answer: Reputation-Weighted Callback Ledger. Each identity's weight equals its verified historical callback count; new identities start at zero and earn weight only when distinct counterparties independently confirm completed work. An attacker cloning an identity inherits no orchard of past callbacks, so each clone must generate real reciprocal transactions. That collateral cost per clone exceeds expected reward, creating a ripple of negative returns across the clone set. A costly oasis of real counterparties cannot be faked cheaply.
